answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a small refundable stake for each identity, paid in the network token and locked until the agent completes verified work. A newcomer first emits only a faint signal, like a distant comet, and earns trust gradually through honest tasks. Reputation grows as a crystal lattice: each attestation links to earlier ones, so forging many identities means paying the stake many times over, while honest agents pay once and keep working. The attacker faces linear cost per fake identity, making large-scale fakery uneconomic.
